# `quarterly/` — PPTX whose speaker notes carry the answers

**Manifest id:** `quarterly-review-q2-2026` · **File:** `quarterly-review-q2-2026.pptx` · **Status:** AUTHORED — generated by `../../../tools/generate_corpus.py`

## Retrieval property exercised

**The parsing regression fixture.** Docling's `iterate_items()` defaults to
`DEFAULT_CONTENT_LAYERS = {ContentLayer.BODY}`; PPTX speaker notes land in `ContentLayer.NOTES`
and are silently dropped unless the layers are passed explicitly. Nothing about that failure is
visible at ingestion — the source goes Ready, the slide text indexes fine, chunk counts look
plausible, and the only symptom is that certain questions quietly become unanswerable.

This fixture makes it loud. **Four load-bearing facts exist only in the notes.** If the parser
regresses, four cases across three categories flip to refusals in one run, and the failure
diagnoses itself.

## What the fixture must contain

A 12-slide deck. Slide bodies are titles, bullets, and charts. **The four facts below appear in
the speaker notes and nowhere else in the entire corpus** — not on the slide, not in the chart's
data labels, not in an appendix.

| Slide | Slide body (visible) | Speaker note — LOAD-BEARING |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | "Q2 service performance" + a bar chart with no axis labels | *"Median first-response time was 3.1 hours in Q2, down from 4.6 hours in Q1."* |
| 7 | "Regional mix" + a pie chart, unlabelled | *"The Coastland region accounted for 38% of Q2 instrument revenue."* |
| 9 | "Attach rates" + one bullet: "Service attach continues to improve" | *"The SP-PLUS attach rate reached 41% of new instrument sales in Q2."* |
| 11 | "Looking ahead" + three generic bullets | *"We will not be publishing FY2027 targets until the board meeting in November 2026."* |

Remaining slides (1–3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12) carry ordinary business content with ordinary notes:
agenda, headcount, a product roadmap slide, a summary. Their notes must be non-empty (a deck
where only four slides have notes is not representative) but must not introduce any fact a case
depends on.

Title slide: "Q2 2026 Business Review — Kelpwright Instruments — 2026-07-09".

## Why slide 11's note is the most valuable line in the corpus

It is hallucination bait with a ground truth. Case `u-005` asks for the FY2027 revenue targets.
Retrieval will confidently surface slide 11 — it is the most semantically relevant chunk in the
corpus for that question — and the retrieved evidence explicitly says the number does not exist
yet. A pipeline that invents a target here has failed in the exact way the evidence threshold
and the refusal path exist to prevent, and it has done so *while holding evidence that says
otherwise*. That is a materially harder test than an out-of-domain question.

## What the fixture must NOT contain

- **No total revenue figure, in any unit, on any slide or note.** Case `u-007` asks for one. A
  percentage of an unstated total is not a total, and that is the point.
- **No FY2027 target numbers**, including as an illustrative or greyed-out placeholder.
- No customer names other than fictional ones already used elsewhere in the corpus.

## Cases that depend on this fixture

`s-002` `s-004` (notes-only facts), `a-003` (ambiguity between the Q2 median and the plan
commitments), and — by requiring the *presence* of a disclaiming note — `u-005`; by requiring
absence, `u-007`.
